$comment: CI admission budget on the liskov CI node. cdk8s builds the Kueue ClusterQueue and the Woodpecker agent's workflow cap from this file, and scripts/checks/ci/check-ci-admission-budget.ts proves the generated pipeline fits it. Quotas sit below liskov's allocatable (29 CPU, ~91.5Gi) on purpose: CPU follows the same rule (every queue, 24 aggregate + 1 maintenance + 2 Delivery, plus about 1.8 of resident requests, <= 29), and every queue plus buildkitd's requests must fit the allocatable memory, so a pod Kueue admits can always schedule. Delivery's executor reserve (2 CPU, 8Gi) is a separate Kueue queue beside this budget, so computeQuota.memory gives up the same 8Gi. The quota is not where the overcommit lives: step requests are sized from measured usage (p90 memory, see the pipeline generator's tiers.ts), and limits stay the per-container backstop above them. The pool workflow caps are a backstop above Kueue's resource admission: an agent holds a workflow's slot while Kueue gates its pod, so the pr cap is sized so that Kueue, not the agent's first-in-first-out queue, orders waiting PR work. With right-sized requests, three verify pods plus a dozen small workflows fit at once, so the pr cap is 12; the main pool is 10 so 17-workflow main pipelines do not wait behind FIFO slots.
